principles: Order stages by how often the situation arises unattended, how clearly the decision is defined, how measurable the outcome is, and how small the interface change is.
Every stage keeps the current rule as the baseline and the fallback, and advances only on a paired gain on held-out seeds.
One shared network per role family; individuals differ through inputs.
The validator owns legality; the network only chooses among legal options.

stages.name: Food-relief exchange
stages.decision: Ask, offer, counter, accept or decline food between two people who share a place.
observation: store stock, reserve target, unit price
options: 12 intents (request, offer, counter, accept, decline, condition, recall, thank, end) as at most 16 legal candidates
outcome: hunger relieved now and a week later

interface.note: In-process crowd harness (crowdsim/fastworld/crowd); probes remain the reference.

stages.size_hint: 5M policy; a 1,321-weight scorer already matches it
stages.first_experiment: Done: hand-written rule, counterfactual labels and evolution all reach +0.032 over the teacher on held-out crowds.
stages.gate: Reached: paired gain over the teacher, better in 31 crowds and worse in 0. The ceiling for this view and objective.
risks: Ceiling reached: more work here buys nothing without a richer view or objective.

stages.name: Villager daily life
stages.decision: What to do today: work, seek aid, buy a meal, lodge, travel, hide, or join a bandit group.
observation: purse, hunger days, unsheltered nights, stress
options: travel destination among neighbouring towns (only when the rule decides to go)
buy the cheapest meal or go without
pay for a bed or sleep rough
join a bandit camp or hold out (left with the rule: story-critical)
outcome: recruitment into bandit groups (17.7 people per world are hiding)

interface.note: CcSimSetPolicy (src/sim/cc_policy.h): the rule computes its legal options and its own choice, then an optional process-wide hook may pick another legal option. Sites: weekly travel destination, meal, lodging, bandit join. With no hook, or one returning the default, the state hash is unchanged (tests/policy_hook_tests.c).

stages.size_hint: A shared 833-weight scorer in C (zero weights reproduce the rule); 5M is not needed
stages.first_experiment: Done: evolved a shared scorer against a season of welfare in 60 worlds; three seeds, then again on the final layout, tested on 100 held-out worlds.
stages.gate: Reached: paired welfare gain over the rule on held-out seeds (z >= 3), bandit membership down, money conserved by construction. Watch stress.
risks: Reward hacking: an unconstrained brain stopped travelling (residents at home are reset to fed) and refused every bandit camp. Travel frequency now stays with the rule and movement is a tracked invariant.
Bandit recruitment is story-critical and stays with the rule; the brain lowers it indirectly by lowering hunger.
Only about 60 road-going people per world face these choices.
stages.result: Welfare +0.14 to +0.16 over the rule (z 29 to 33), better in 100 of 100 held-out worlds every time. Road-going people are hungry 5 points less (21.7% to about 16.7%) and outlawed 9 points less (14.1% to about 5%). The gain comes only from where travellers go (30% of destination picks change); meals and beds never change. Stress rises about 1 point (z up to 6). Movement rises 12 to 17%.

stages.name: Gossip and requests
stages.decision: What to tell, how to retell it, whom to believe, and which personal request to make or answer.
observation: held accounts with source, certainty and age
own occupation and needs (bread, wheat, iron, wood, repairs)
options: share, withhold or distort an account (retellings change counts, people, directions or motives)
report, keep confidence, pledge help or listen (four responses)
ask for or fulfil an item request
outcome: accuracy of what the town believes about real events

interface.note: Hook at the point a carrier shares a story with a town (share or withhold). Carriers include couriers and carriages, not only characters.

stages.size_hint: 5M; the typed fact-selection pilot already targets this
stages.first_experiment: Done: hook, informedness metric (coverage times accuracy), a threshold sweep and an evolution run.
stages.gate: Not reached: no policy raises accuracy at equal reach. The rule sits on the frontier. Personal requests and the player-facing responses are not covered.
risks: Fluency is not truth: the validator must own what may be said.
Scoring accuracy needs a ground-truth event log per world.
stages.result: No gain. Withholding shaky stories raises accuracy (77.5% to 87.1% at a floor of 80) but coverage falls faster (67.7% to 50.6%); the combined score is flat at best. 150 generations of evolution found nothing better than "always share". The trade-off is real, so gossip reliability is a candidate personality trait rather than something to optimise.

stages.name: Trade, shipments and production
stages.decision: Which good to move, where, how much, and what to produce; how a carriage picks its next job.
observation: stock, reserve target and price by settlement and good
options: ship, hold or fund grain supply
carriage mode: idle, repositioning, delivering, blocked, waiting for capacity, road repair
route choice (CcTradeFindPath)
outcome: shipments lost (17 per world) and delivered (127)

interface.note: Hook at the royal carriage trade planner: it offers every legal (good, source, destination) the rule scored above zero, defaulting to the rule's argmax.

stages.size_hint: 1M to 5M; small state, many repeated decisions
stages.first_experiment: Done: hook, town hunger and famine metrics, a bias sweep and evolution runs.
stages.gate: Reached, modestly: a paired gain on 400 held-out worlds (z = 3.6) with the rule's legality unchanged. One search, one seed; outcomes vary by 8 hunger points between worlds.
risks: Economy tuning is delicate and player-facing; keep the rule as a fallback and shadow-test first.
stages.result: A small gain on 400 fresh worlds: town welfare +0.0167 +- 0.0046 (z = 3.6), famine 20.5% to about 19.4% of town-days (z = -4.1), hunger -0.52 of 13.1 (z = -2.9), better in 239 of 400. Single-parameter tweaks of the rule's score (hungry destinations, need, distance) were neutral or worse, so it comes from a combination of features. A short first search was level with the rule, and a 100-world check was marginal, so the result needed the larger test. Famine still covers about a fifth of town-days: allocation is not the main driver.

stages.name: Raiders and monsters
stages.decision: Whether, when and where to raid; what to take; whether to pay or take tribute.
observation: own members, supplies, coins, camp size
target settlement stock, guards and route danger
goblin motive: hunger, equipment or dragon tribute
options: bandit raid phases: idle, scouting, mustering, outbound, returning
raid target, good and quantity
goblin tribute phases: idle, outbound, returning, to dragon, preparing

interface.note: Hooks in the bandit raid launcher (raid or hold) and its choice of town. Goblin raids are a separate path and are not hooked.

stages.size_hint: 5M; two-sided, so raiders and defenders co-evolve
stages.first_experiment: Done: hooks, a never-raid bound and an evolution run.
stages.gate: Not reached: no gain. The two-sided worry (raiders stripping towns) does not arise in this sim.
risks: Adversarial: optimising raiders alone will strip the world; needs a two-sided or bounded objective.
Unattended raids are rare per seed (about one bandit group per world).
stages.result: Null. Raids barely touch the towns: with no raids at all, hunger changes by -0.03 and prosperity rises by 0.9 of 66. Under an even balance of loot and prosperity a search gave +0.04 +- 0.04 (z = 1.1). The rule already takes the town with the most stock.

stages.name: Kingdoms and war
stages.decision: What a kingdom does with its treasury and legitimacy, which factions to back, and how a war party is ordered.
observation: diplomatic state (peace, war, alliance) with each neighbour
options: war orders: hold, march, control route, withdraw, cease
fund the war chest, buy supply, back or shift a faction
succession and pretender responses
outcome: wars avoided or won at low cost

interface.note: Hook at the kingdom's grain relief: any hungry town of the kingdom, or hold the treasury. War orders and succession are not hooked.

stages.size_hint: 5M to 10M; long horizons and sparse rewards
stages.first_experiment: Done: hook, realm metrics (legitimacy, treasury, hunger, famine) and a two-stage evaluation.
stages.gate: Not reached. War orders are untested and need an injected scenario.
risks: Sparse and delayed reward; needs scenario injection to see enough wars.
Story-critical: authored beats must not be optimised away.
stages.result: Null. Relief spending is a small lever (never spending raises hunger by 0.63 of 13.1). A search that looked promising on 100 worlds was slightly worse on 400 fresh ones (welfare -0.007, z = -2.0), so the rule (fund the hungriest) stands. War could not be tested: WAR_DECLARED never fires unattended.

stages.name: Dragons
stages.decision: Hunt, retaliate, brood or lie dormant; whom to retaliate against; when to campaign.
observation: life stage, body condition, crown strength, memory integrity
options: activity: dormant, hunting, retaliating, brooding, aftermath
retaliation target
campaign phase: idle, outbound, returning
outcome: story pacing: an omen and a reckoning that make sense

interface.note: Hook at the dragon's choice of town to burn, plus an injected-theft harness (dragons retaliate only 0.4 times per world unattended). Hunting, brooding and campaigns are not hooked.

stages.size_hint: Start at 5M; scale to 10M-50M only if the option space and reward become rich. The one measured 5M-to-50M comparison (byte language modelling) gained 11% for ten times the parameters
stages.first_experiment: Done: injected 300-crown thefts and forced each candidate town over 100 worlds.
stages.gate: Half reached: paired scenario outcomes are measured; the authored-story review (does an omen and a reckoning still make sense?) is not done.
risks: Rarity: little natural data, so scenario design carries the result.
Highest player impact; keep the validator gate and a safe default action.
stages.result: The dragon collects the same restitution (about 349 crowns) whichever town burns, so its own payoff gives no reason to prefer a target. The rule's target (the richest town) is the most damaging: 40 to 60% fewer people are lost in the alternatives at the same payoff. Vengeful or restrained is an authorial choice, so it is a personality axis for L7, not an optimisation target.

stages.name: Lineages and open-ended evolution
stages.decision: How inherited traits bias the shared brain across generations.
observation: the L1-L2 inputs plus a small inherited trait vector
options: the same options as the stage each individual acts in
outcome: diversity of behaviour across the population

interface.note: Per-person trait rows (rich, cheap, near, home towns) bias the shared brain's travel scores; successors inherit with mutation. Successions in this sim are replacements in the same slot, born as age-0 children, and nothing in the sim selects on traits, so selection is added by the harness.

stages.size_hint: One shared brain plus a per-person trait vector
stages.first_experiment: Done: lineage.py with three conditions (none, drift, selection) over 12 accelerated years and, for comparison, 300 and 1000 natural years.
stages.gate: Weakly reached: diversity sustained without loss of welfare. It does not show that selection helps.
risks: Unattended worlds lose every road within about 20 years, so anything about travel is only meaningful for the first 10 to 15 years; a 1,000-year run had 13 generations but no travel after year 50, and so no selection.
Successors are born as children who cannot travel for 16 years; accelerated generations seat them as adults.
Traits have a small effect on outcomes; a richer fitness (scarcity, competition) is needed for open-ended evolution.
stages.result: With generations accelerated (lifespans 1.5 to 3 years, successors seated as adults; about 4.7 generations in 12 years, 32 worlds) diversity is sustained (trait spread 0.49 to 0.56) and welfare is not lost (selection versus brain alone -0.002 +- 0.006). Selection is only marginally better than neutral drift (-0.009 +- 0.005, z = -1.8) and trait means barely move, so there is no directional evolution to report.

tracks.name: Policy hook
tracks.goal: One interface for every stage: observation, legal options, apply, outcome, with the rule as the default.
have: CcSimSetPolicy decision hook at 10 sites with a hash-invariance test
in-process food-relief and daily-life worlds (about 28,000 simulated days per second)
need: the hook is process-wide and single-threaded
goblin raids, war orders, hunting, brooding, personal requests

tracks.name: Evaluation
tracks.goal: Judge on outcomes, on held-out seeds, paired against the current rule.
have: a movement invariant that caught a reward hack
need: story review for dragons and kingdoms

tracks.name: Determinism
tracks.goal: Identical choices on arm64, x86-64 and WebAssembly.
have: byte-exact native parity checks against the float path
need: an integer forward pass (RoPE, SiLU table, head_dim 32)

tracks.name: Runtime and sizes
tracks.goal: Load several small models by role.
need: exporter limits above dim 256 and 16 layers for larger models

tracks.name: Reward hygiene
need: a KL anchor to the rule when learning from outcomes

findings: L1 shows a clear gain over the rule and L3 a small one. L2, L4 and L5 are nulls, L6 is a design axis and L7 holds only weakly. The hand-written rules are close to a local optimum for the objectives measured, except where they choose at random (travel destination).

A reward hack appeared at once: an unconstrained daily-life brain stopped travelling (residents at home are reset to fed) and refused every bandit camp. Fixing the rule's decision to go, leaving story-critical choices with the rule, and tracking movement as an invariant closed it.

Small effects need many worlds, in both directions. A 100-world hint at L5 reversed on 400 fresh worlds, while a marginal 100-world result at L3 became significant on 400. Town outcomes vary by 8 hunger points between worlds.

The unattended sim decays: every road closes within about 20 years, two of six towns are abandoned by year 100, and successors are born as age-0 children. Long-horizon experiments are only valid for the first 10 to 15 simulated years.
